nodes.label: Compliance vs. Sensibility: Reasoning Controllability in LLMs
nodes.author: Xingwei Tan et al.
nodes.rationale: Investigates tension between instruction compliance and logical sensibility in LLM reasoning, using mechanistic analysis and steering to enhance reasoning controllability.

nodes.label: Reasoning Conflict Framework
nodes.rationale: Framework for evaluating tension between instruction compliance and logical sensibility in LLM reasoning, classifying responses into sensible/compliant/both/neither categories.

nodes.label: Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA)
nodes.rationale: Model steering technique modifying internal activations during inference to enhance reasoning compliance without parameter updates, achieving up to 29% improvement.

nodes.label: Mechanistic Interpretation of Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Analysis combining linear probing and CKA to reveal instruction decodability and geometric differences in reasoning representations across models and layers.

nodes.label: Dominant Reasoning Mode Assumption
nodes.rationale: Controlled testbed assumption that most prominent reasoning type contributing to final answer is classified, enabling systematic evaluation of reasoning conflicts.

nodes.label: Lexical Mimicking in Reasoning Classification
nodes.rationale: Frontier models superficially echo reasoning instruction terms without executing corresponding logical operations, requiring rule-based parser verification.

nodes.label: Compliance-Sensibility Response Categories
nodes.rationale: Four categories: Sensible∩Compliant, Sensible∩¬Compliant, ¬Sensible∩Compliant, ¬Sensible∩¬Compliant for systematic reasoning conflict analysis.

nodes.label: Confidence Drop During Reasoning Conflicts
nodes.rationale: Reasoning conflicts are internally detectable via confidence score drops, enabling identification of conflicting episodes.

nodes.label: Instruction Decodability via Linear Probing
nodes.rationale: Linear probing reveals instruction decodability even in non-compliant responses, indicating instructions are processed but not followed.

nodes.label: CKA Geometric Analysis of Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Centered Kernel Alignment identifies geometric differences in reasoning representations across models and layers.

nodes.label: Steering Vector Generation
nodes.rationale: Mean difference of residual stream activations between compliant and non-compliant response pairs, controlling intensity via coefficient μ.

nodes.label: Cohen's κ Agreement in Reasoning Classification
nodes.rationale: Human-GPT5.1 agreement κ=0.84 for reasoning type classification, validating LLM-as-Judge framework with rule-based parser.

nodes.label: Reasoning Conflict in LLMs
nodes.author: Tan et al.
nodes.rationale: Core finding: LLMs prioritize logical sensibility over instruction compliance, with models opting for task-appropriate reasoning 43.5% of the time vs. following instructions at expense of task appropriateness only 18.6% of the time.

nodes.label: FOLIO Dataset (Deduction)
nodes.rationale: First-order logic dataset for evaluating deductive reasoning; models must determine truth value of claims based on logical constraints.

nodes.label: SPR Dataset (Induction)
nodes.rationale: Sequence Pattern Recognition task requiring models to predict next element in numerical sequences; proxy for inductive reasoning.

nodes.label: αNLI Dataset (Abduction)
nodes.rationale: Abductive Natural Language Inference dataset presenting story beginning/ending; requires selecting plausible intermediate hypothesis.

nodes.label: RECV Dataset (Mixed Reasoning)
nodes.rationale: Real-world claim verification from Wikipedia/Twitter with human-annotated reasoning types; diverse testbed for reasoning compliance.

nodes.label: Sensibility vs Compliance Trade-off
nodes.rationale: Key tension: models achieve higher accuracy when reasoning is sensible (S∩C and S∩¬C) regardless of compliance; compliance correlates with internal confidence but not accuracy.

nodes.label: P(True) Confidence Estimation
nodes.rationale: Method to measure model confidence by asking follow-up question about answer truth value; reveals subtle friction from reasoning conflicts even when not catastrophic.

nodes.label: Linear Probing of Hidden States
nodes.rationale: Mechanistic analysis: trains linear probes on residual stream activations to predict instructed reasoning type, judge-inferred type, and compliance; shows instruction encoding is robust but compliance is weaker signal.

nodes.label: Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) Analysis
nodes.rationale: Representation similarity analysis across reasoning instructions; reveals instruction-dependent geometry differences vary by model family (LLaMA shows largest differences, Qwen shows transient dips).

nodes.label: Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA) Steering
nodes.rationale: Intervention technique to steer model compliance by applying steering vectors to specific layers; increases compliance up to 29% but reveals task-neglect side effects and accuracy trade-offs.

nodes.label: Model Scale and Reasoning Properties
nodes.rationale: Larger models show higher sensibility but compliance is family-dependent and parameter-agnostic; architectural choices and instruction-tuning recipes matter more than scale for compliance.

nodes.label: Built-in Thinking Mode Effects
nodes.rationale: Models with thinking mode (Qwen, OLMo) show higher sensibility but lower compliance; indicates substantial behavior difference between internal thinking and external CoT.

nodes.label: Lexical Mirroring Phenomenon
nodes.rationale: Models incorporate key terminology from prompts (e.g., 'most probable', 'simplest hypothesis') to signal compliance while internally pivoting to different reasoning type; masks true reasoning process.

nodes.label: GPT-5.1 Model
nodes.rationale: Largest evaluated model; exhibits highest sensibility (88.1%) but used as judge for other models; demonstrates scaling trend in logical grounding.

nodes.label: LLaMA Model Family
nodes.rationale: Shows inverse scaling for compliance: LLaMA3.1-8B-IT (65.1% compliance) more compliant than LLaMA3.3-70B-IT; suggests post-training methodology dominates scale.

nodes.label: Qwen Model Family
nodes.rationale: Thinking mode on increases sensibility but decreases compliance; 4x parameter increase (8B→32B) shows standard scaling for compliance; demonstrates architectural effects.

nodes.label: OLMo Model Family
nodes.rationale: OLMo3-7B-IT shows lowest compliance (39%); thinking mode reduces compliance further; used for steering experiments due to low baseline compliance.

nodes.label: Gemini 3 Flash Model
nodes.rationale: Underperforms relative to parameter class; trails LLaMA3.3-70B-IT and OLMo3.1-32B-IT; suggests architectural/training choices affect reasoning properties.

nodes.label: Accuracy Driven by Sensibility
nodes.rationale: Key finding: task accuracy correlates with sensibility (S∩C and S∩¬C cohorts) regardless of compliance; sensible/non-compliant often outperforms compliant/non-sensible.

nodes.label: FOLIO Accuracy Gap
nodes.rationale: Sensible CoT maintains 20-40% accuracy lead over compliant/non-sensible on FOLIO; largest disparity among datasets; deduction task most sensitive to reasoning type.

nodes.label: RECV Marginal Accuracy Gap
nodes.rationale: Real-world claim verification shows <20% accuracy differences across categories; suggests mixed reasoning types less sensitive to compliance than pure deduction.
